churn_resistance.rationale: The layering is genuinely good — one data module, one boundary file, one config file, boilerplate identical to the current v2 template — but 'types at boundaries' is the criterion's headline construct and it is almost entirely absent: `any` from fetch through to the JSX, with `tsc --noEmit` never run in the build, so changes in the API or the loader contract surface at runtime. Combined with the A-per-link pattern, a router upgrade would touch every view.

findings.issue: The entire data contract is `any`: fetchApi returns Promise<any>, every loader returns untyped objects, and components re-cast them (`app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:154`, `app/src/routes/index.tsx:49`, 40+ total), despite "strict": true at app/tsconfig.json:12 — and nothing ever runs tsc, since `build` is plain `vite build`.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for each loader's return value (Species, PokemonCard, MoveRow…) and for the PokeAPI resources, type the queries with them, and add a `typecheck` script (`tsc --noEmit`) to CI.

findings.issue: `A` is used for every internal link (~30 sites: app.tsx, PokemonCard.tsx, all route files), but docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/components/a states "A will be deprecated in favor of the native <a> element".
findings.suggestion: Use plain `<a href>` — Solid Router's delegated click handling soft-navigates native anchors — keeping at most the header nav on `A` if active-class styling is ever wanted (the app never styles .active).

findings.issue: The 404 page renders markup only; the response status stays 200. The current `HttpStatusCode` API from `@solidjs/start` is unused even though the SSR mode it needs (`mode: "async"`) is already set at app/src/entry-server.tsx:22.
findings.suggestion: Add `<HttpStatusCode code={404} />` to the NotFound component (spec says a 404 status is encouraged).

findings.issue: `createHandler(..., { mode: "async" })` overrides the v2 default `"stream"`, so data-heavy pages (the home route ships all 1,025 species) are fully buffered before the first byte of HTML.
findings.suggestion: Drop the options object (or use "stream") so Suspense can flush the shell early; async is only needed if you keep relying on HttpStatusCode semantics that streaming doesn't support.

findings.issue: `idFromUrl` strips trailing slashes and splits strings by hand to extract an ID.
findings.suggestion: Use `new URL(url).pathname` and take the last segment — it also validates the URL shape for free.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or AbortController, and the in-memory cache stores a promise per path with no eviction (app/src/lib/api.ts:21-24), so a slow API can pin requests indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass an AbortSignal with a timeout to fetch and let the cache evict on abort, as well as on error.

findings.issue: There is no ErrorBoundary anywhere; the v2 data-fetching guide shows queries wrapped in ErrorBoundary, and a non-404 API error currently produces an unhandled server error.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the Suspense children in an ErrorBoundary with a small fallback component.

findings.issue: Route components hand-roll the props type (`props: { params: { name: string } }`) instead of importing the router's `RouteSectionProps`, duplicating a framework type in all four param routes.
findings.suggestion: Type route components with `RouteSectionProps` from @solidjs/router so param typing stays framework-owned.

findings.issue: `vite` and `nitro` are runtime `dependencies`; they are build-time tools and Nitro's node-server output is self-contained, so production installs pull them in for nothing.
findings.suggestion: Move both to devDependencies — the docs' `npm i` command puts them in dependencies, but they are never imported at runtime.

findings.issue: The production build directory lives inside app/ and is not covered by the repo .gitignore (which only ignores /data/, /.data-cache/, node_modules/), so built artifacts can be committed.
findings.suggestion: Add `.output/` to a gitignore inside app/.

summary: This is an unusually current codebase: SolidStart v2 with the documented Vite-8/Nitro-v3 setup, Router 1.x query/preload/createAsync, and every dependency at the latest published version, with all data access isolated behind one server module and one query boundary. It loses points on the two things most likely to bite in a year: the data contract is untyped `any` end-to-end (strict tsconfig never actually enforced by any build step), and every link uses `A`, which the current router docs flag for deprecation in favor of native anchors. I'd approve it with the typing and anchor changes requested before merge.
